rationale: C07 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Although it concerns Luxembourg trademarks rather than Australian copyrights, it uses the same distinctive administrative machinery and closely parallel operative language: presidential authority to extend time for foreign nationals receiving substantially equal treatment; a finding that wartime disruption or suspension of essential facilities prevented compliance with statutory conditions and formalities; a conclusion that the affected rights fall within the governing statute; and an extension of the compliance period. C11 and C14 are essentially equivalent instances of that template, but C07 is ranked first. C01 shares the copyright regime and reciprocity background but expressly concerns ordinary copyright eligibility and excludes the extension-of-time benefit, so it is a weaker drafting analogue than the extension proclamations.
